youtube_title: How does regenerative braking work in EVs?
caption:
Regenerative braking turns your motor into a generator when you slow down, sending energy back to the battery. That's why EVs and strong hybrids love stop-go city traffic, and why it doesn't add much on a steady highway run.

One safety note: one-pedal or strong regen modes are great, but keep your foot ready for the brake pedal. Regen alone won't do an emergency stop.

Do you drive in one-pedal mode? Tell me below 👇

slides.heading: Regen adds big range on highways
Only when you slow down
slides.body: Regen turns braking into charge. Steady highway cruising means little braking, so little gain.

slides.heading: City traffic is where it shines
slides.body: Stop-go traffic means constant slowing. One-pedal mode recovers energy brakes would waste as heat.

slides.heading: Hybrids do it too
slides.body: Strong hybrids store braking energy in their battery to drive on electric at low speeds.

slides.heading: Lift off early, brake less
slides.body: Red signal ahead? Lift off early and let regen slow you. Saves energy and brake pads.

voice_lines: Does regen add big range on highways? Not really. It only makes charge when you slow down.
In city traffic you're slowing all the time, so one pedal mode keeps recovering energy that brakes would waste.
Hybrids do the same trick, storing braking energy in their battery to drive on electric at low speeds.
My tip: see a red light ahead, lift off early and let regen slow you. Follow for more EV tips.
